about.title: Rancho Santa Margarita Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Rancho Santa Margarita is a small city by Orange County standards — just over 49,000 residents — and in 2025 it recorded 54 injury collisions, 73 people hurt, and one traffic death. When a life is lost on Santa Margarita Parkway, Antonio Parkway, Avenida De Las Flores or Alma Aldea because of someone's carelessness, the people left behind face decisions no one is prepared for. California's wrongful death law exists for those decisions. It lets a spouse or domestic partner, children, and in some cases other dependents or heirs bring a civil claim for funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. That claim runs on its own track, separate from any criminal case, and it generally must be filed within two years of the death — sooner if a public agency is involved. Our team handles wrongful death claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Rancho Santa Margarita Families Choose Us

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim — a spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. We can sort out your family's standing before anything else is decided.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general filing window is two years from the date of death, and it shrinks considerably when a city, county or state agency may be responsible. Acting sooner keeps those options open.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: We handle wrongful death cases on contingency. Your family should not have to weigh legal bills against grief.

items.question: The crash happened on Santa Margarita Parkway and the other driver was cited. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, if your family wants to recover losses. A traffic citation or criminal charge is handled by the state and does not compensate survivors. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action that addresses funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love and companionship, and it can move forward regardless of what happens in a criminal court.

items.question: How long do we have to act in Orange County?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity — such as a public agency responsible for a roadway or vehicle — may share fault, a claim usually has to be presented much sooner. We can confirm which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What does it cost to work with you?
items.answer: There is no charge for a consultation. We take wrongful death cases on contingency, so no fee is owed unless there is a recovery.
